text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistan and India said they hoped to produce "an agreed document" at the end of three days of talks on Sunday.
- Pakistani President Farooq Leghari and Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif advised India to avoid taking what they called negative factors so peace talks could succeed.
- Plans to make cheap money available for the private sector may not succeed as the public sector borrowing is likely to eat up more from the banking sector than is being projected.

- Pakistan is threatened by a possible reimposition of differential or Cumulative Recovery System of duty on husked and basmati rice exports, following the European Commission's tentative conclusion that Pakistan has not honoured its commitment on quality and inspection.
- The steel industry has received the largest chunk of incentives provided under restructured tariff which is part of the federal budget for 1997/98 (July-June).
- The Central Depository Company Ltd will start operation from September 3.
- Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz has convened a meeting on June 24 in Islamabad to discuss the levy of three percent turnover tax or general sales tax at the retail level.
- Sybase Inc, an American database and front end software tool company, has launched its products in Pakistan.
- The Prime Minister has directed the Privatisation Commission to privatise all state-owned financial institutions by March 1998.
- Pakistan Railways needs $900 million investment for additional locomotives and wagons within five to 10 years to make it a customer-oriented and reliable rail service.

- Aziz has said the budget strategy adopted by the present government involved a "calculated and not a wild risk" and expressed the confidence that the sagging economy would be successfully rehabilitated.
- The fertiliser import bill is expected to reach more than $3 billion in 1997/98 due to increase in the prices of fertilisers in the international markets.

- General Hameed Gul, former director general of Inter Services Intelligence, the military spy agency, has decided to go to court against bypassing of extradition treaty between Pakistan and the United States in the case of Mir Aimal Kansi.
